headline: Afghan cyclist wins silver medal after training in disguise
meta_description: Fariba Hashimi, who disguised herself as a man to train safely in Afghanistan, has won silver at the Asian Games near Nagoya, Japan.
summary_short: A 23-year-old Afghan cyclist who once dressed as a man to avoid Taliban attacks has earned a silver medal at the Asian Games, inspiring hope for the next generation.
body:
Fariba Hashimi, a 23-year-old cyclist from Afghanistan, has claimed a silver medal in the women's road race at the Asian Games near Nagoya, Japan. Her achievement is remarkable not only for the medal itself, but for the journey that brought her to this moment: before fleeing Afghanistan after the Taliban returned to power in 2021, Hashimi trained in disguise, wearing multiple masks and men's clothing to avoid being attacked while pursuing her passion for cycling in her home province of Faryab. "I was born inside a country where the women who dream are getting attacked," she reflected on her victory, "and I'm really happy that I have fought against that."

The silver medal marks the culmination of years of quiet resistance. During training rides in Afghanistan, Hashimi had to navigate not just physical danger but constant harassment—stones thrown at her as she cycled. Her determination mirrors that of her sister Yulduz, also an international cyclist, who inspired Hashimi to begin racing at age 15 despite the risks. Both sisters eventually found safety and opportunity abroad, with Hashimi now training in Italy under the mentorship of Alessandra Cappellotto, an Italian former world champion.

Today, Hashimi's resilience extends beyond personal achievement. She views her medal as a symbol for millions of Afghan women facing restrictions on their freedoms. "This silver medal can show a lot of resilience from Afghan women," she said, speaking to the broader struggle of women whose dreams have been constrained by circumstance. With her sister, she competed at the 2024 Paris Olympics and has already set her sights on the 2028 Los Angeles Games. "I hope that the next generation will come here and represent their country without any fear," Hashimi said—a quiet but powerful statement of hope for a future where such courage is no longer necessary.
quick_facts: 23-year-old Afghan cyclist won silver at Asian Games in Japan
Once trained wearing masks and men's clothing to avoid attacks
Now trains in Italy with help from Italian world champion
Competed at 2024 Paris Olympics with her sister Yulduz
Fled Afghanistan after Taliban returned to power in 2021
